from dataclasses import dataclass

RULES = ("keep_last", "keep_daily", "keep_weekly", "keep_monthly", "keep_yearly")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Policy:
    """Retention settings, as read from the `retention` section of a vaultsnap config file.

    The meaning of every field is decided in docs/adr/. This class only validates the values.
    """

    keep_last: int = None
    keep_daily: int = None
    keep_weekly: int = None
    keep_monthly: int = None
    keep_yearly: int = None
    protect_tags: frozenset = frozenset()
    tz_offset_minutes: int = 0
    day_start_hour: int = 0

    def __post_init__(self):
        for name in RULES:
            value = getattr(self, name)
            if value is not None and (isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 0):
                raise ValueError(f"{name} must be a whole number of at least 0 or None, got {value!r}")
        object.__setattr__(self, "protect_tags", frozenset(self.protect_tags))
        offset = self.tz_offset_minutes
        if isinstance(offset, bool) or not isinstance(offset, int) or not -720 <= offset <= 840:
            raise ValueError(f"tz_offset_minutes must be a whole number between -720 and 840, got {offset!r}")
        hour = self.day_start_hour
        if isinstance(hour, bool) or not isinstance(hour, int) or not 0 <= hour <= 23:
            raise ValueError(f"day_start_hour must be a whole number between 0 and 23, got {hour!r}")

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, data):
        known = set(RULES) | {"protect_tags", "tz_offset_minutes", "day_start_hour"}
        unknown = sorted(set(data) - known)
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown retention settings: {unknown}")
        return cls(**data)

    @property
    def has_rules(self):
        """True when at least one keep_* rule is switched on (a value of None or 0 is off)."""
        return any(getattr(self, name) for name in RULES)
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Plan:

    Both lists are ordered newest first.

    keep: list
    prune: list


def plan_retention(snapshots, policy, now):
    """Decide which snapshots to keep and which to prune. Nothing is deleted here; this only plans.

    raise NotImplementedError

# ADR-0001: Retention model

Status: Accepted. The section "Weeks" below is superseded by ADR-0003. The section "Day boundaries" defers to ADR-0002, which is itself superseded (see there).

Date: 2026-01-12

## Context

`vaultsnap` keeps one snapshot per nightly run, plus ad-hoc snapshots taken before risky changes. Disk space is finite, so old snapshots are pruned. A pruned snapshot is gone for good, so the rules must be exact.

## Decision

### Inputs

`plan_retention(snapshots, policy, now)` takes snapshots (id, `taken_at`, tags), a policy and `now`. Every datetime, including `now`, must be timezone-aware; a naive datetime raises `ValueError`. Two snapshots with the same id raise `ValueError`. The function only plans; it never deletes.

### Ordering

"Newer" means a later `taken_at`; when two snapshots have the same `taken_at`, the one with the greater id (plain string comparison) is the newer.

### Rules

The policy has five counted rules: `keep_last`, `keep_daily`, `keep_weekly`, `keep_monthly`, `keep_yearly`. A rule whose value is `None` or `0` is off. If all five rules are off, every snapshot is kept (an empty policy never prunes).

### Set-aside snapshots

Before any rule is applied, two kinds of snapshot are set aside. They are always kept, they do not count toward any rule's N, and they can never be the representative of a bucket (below):

- snapshots that carry at least one tag listed in `protect_tags`;
- snapshots whose `taken_at` is later than `now` (a clock-skew guard). A snapshot taken exactly at `now` is not set aside.

All rules below look only at the remaining snapshots.

### keep_last

`keep_last = N` keeps the N newest remaining snapshots, whatever bucket they are in.

### Buckets (daily, weekly, monthly, yearly)

Each remaining snapshot belongs to one bucket per rule, identified by a key:

| Rule | Bucket key |
|---|---|
| `keep_daily` | the calendar date |
| `keep_weekly` | see "Weeks" |
| `keep_monthly` | (calendar year, calendar month) |
| `keep_yearly` | the calendar year |

The dates and times behind these keys are the snapshot's local time, see "Day boundaries".

`keep_X = N` takes the N newest buckets that contain at least one remaining snapshot, and keeps the newest snapshot of each of those buckets. Periods with no snapshots do not exist as buckets, so they never use up part of N. "Newest bucket" means the greatest key.

The five rules are independent of each other: a snapshot is kept if any rule keeps it, and one rule keeping a snapshot does not change what another rule picks.

### Weeks

Weeks run from Sunday to Saturday. The weekly bucket key is the date of the Sunday that starts the week.

### Day boundaries

Days start where ADR-0002 says they start.

### Output

The result is a `Plan` whose `keep` and `prune` lists together hold every snapshot id exactly once, each list ordered newest first.
# ADR-0002: Bucket boundaries use UTC

Status: Superseded by ADR-0004.

Date: 2026-01-19

## Context

Snapshots are stored with timezone-aware timestamps. Buckets need a day boundary.

## Decision

Every bucket is computed in UTC: a day starts at 00:00 UTC, and the week, month and year keys come from the UTC date.

## Consequences

Simple and the same on every machine. Teams far from UTC see their "daily" bucket split in the middle of their working day.
# ADR-0003: Weekly buckets are ISO weeks

Status: Accepted. Supersedes the section "Weeks" of ADR-0001.

Date: 2026-02-09

## Context

Sunday-start weeks (ADR-0001) disagree with the calendars and reports our users already read, which use ISO 8601 weeks. Around New Year the two also put the same snapshots in different weeks.

## Decision

The weekly bucket key is the ISO calendar pair (ISO year, ISO week number), as `date.isocalendar()` returns it; weeks start on Monday. Buckets are ordered by that pair, so (2026, 1) is newer than (2025, 52).

The ISO year is used only for weekly buckets. Monthly buckets stay (calendar year, calendar month) and yearly buckets stay the calendar year. For example, a snapshot dated 2025-12-30 is in weekly bucket (2026, 1), monthly bucket (2025, 12) and yearly bucket 2025.

Nothing else in ADR-0001 changes.
# ADR-0004: Configurable day boundary

Status: Accepted. Supersedes ADR-0002.

Date: 2026-02-23

## Context

ADR-0002 fixed buckets to UTC. Our nightly job runs at 01:30 to 03:30 local time, so with a UTC day the "daily" bucket put a night's snapshot together with the previous evening's ad-hoc snapshots for some teams and not for others.

## Decision

The policy has two settings that decide where a day starts:

- `tz_offset_minutes`: a fixed offset from UTC in minutes (default 0). It is a plain offset: there is no daylight saving handling and no zone names.
- `day_start_hour`: the local hour at which a day starts, 0 to 23 (default 0).

The bucket time of a snapshot is computed as follows: convert `taken_at` to the fixed offset, then subtract `day_start_hour` hours. The calendar date of the result is the snapshot's date, and the daily, weekly (ADR-0003), monthly and yearly keys are all derived from that one result. So with `day_start_hour = 4`, a snapshot taken at 03:30 local on 1 January belongs to 31 December of the previous year in every rule.

Only the bucket keys use the bucket time. Ordering of snapshots, `keep_last`, and the comparison with `now` use the real instant `taken_at` and are not shifted.

With the defaults (offset 0, hour 0) this is the UTC behaviour of ADR-0002.
import unittest
from datetime import datetime

from vaultsnap import Plan, Policy, Snapshot, plan_retention

NOW = datetime.fromisoformat("2026-03-20T12:00:00+00:00")


def snap(stamp, *tags):
    return Snapshot("s-" + stamp.replace("-", "").replace(":", ""), datetime.fromisoformat(stamp + "+00:00"), frozenset(tags))


def ids(*stamps):
    return ["s-" + s.replace("-", "").replace(":", "") for s in stamps]


class PlanTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_keep_last(self):
        shots = [snap("2026-03-10T03:00"), snap("2026-03-11T03:00"), snap("2026-03-12T03:00"), snap("2026-03-13T03:00")]
        plan = plan_retention(shots, Policy(keep_last=2), NOW)
        self.assertEqual(plan.keep, ids("2026-03-13T03:00", "2026-03-12T03:00"))
        self.assertEqual(plan.prune, ids("2026-03-11T03:00", "2026-03-10T03:00"))

    def test_daily_keeps_the_newest_of_each_day(self):
        shots = [snap("2026-03-17T01:00"), snap("2026-03-17T13:00"), snap("2026-03-18T02:00"), snap("2026-03-18T22:00")]
        plan = plan_retention(shots, Policy(keep_daily=2), NOW)
        self.assertEqual(plan.keep, ids("2026-03-18T22:00", "2026-03-17T13:00"))
        self.assertEqual(plan.prune, ids("2026-03-18T02:00", "2026-03-17T01:00"))

    def test_weekly_keeps_the_newest_of_each_week(self):
        shots = [snap("2026-03-03T03:00"), snap("2026-03-04T03:00"), snap("2026-03-11T03:00"), snap("2026-03-12T03:00")]
        plan = plan_retention(shots, Policy(keep_weekly=2), NOW)
        self.assertEqual(plan.keep, ids("2026-03-12T03:00", "2026-03-04T03:00"))

    def test_protected_tag_is_always_kept(self):
        shots = [snap("2026-03-10T03:00", "release"), snap("2026-03-11T03:00"), snap("2026-03-12T03:00")]
        plan = plan_retention(shots, Policy(keep_last=1, protect_tags={"release"}), NOW)
        self.assertEqual(plan.keep, ids("2026-03-12T03:00", "2026-03-10T03:00"))
        self.assertEqual(plan.prune, ids("2026-03-11T03:00"))

    def test_no_rules_keeps_everything(self):
        shots = [snap("2026-03-10T03:00"), snap("2026-03-11T03:00")]
        plan = plan_retention(shots, Policy(), NOW)
        self.assertEqual(plan.prune, [])
        self.assertEqual(len(plan.keep), 2)

    def test_returns_a_plan_for_no_snapshots(self):
        self.assertEqual(plan_retention([], Policy(keep_last=3), NOW), Plan(keep=[], prune=[]))

    def test_naive_datetimes_are_rejected(self):
        naive = Snapshot("x", datetime(2026, 3, 1, 3, 0))
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            plan_retention([naive], Policy(keep_last=1), NOW)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import unittest
from datetime import datetime, timezone

from vaultsnap import Policy, Snapshot, plan_retention

NOW = datetime(2026, 3, 20, 12, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def S(id, stamp, *tags):
    return Snapshot(id, datetime.fromisoformat(stamp), frozenset(tags))


class AdrTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_iso_week_across_new_year(self):
        shots = [S("a", "2025-12-30T03:00+00:00"), S("b", "2026-01-02T03:00+00:00")]
        plan = plan_retention(shots, Policy(keep_weekly=5), NOW)
        self.assertEqual((plan.keep, plan.prune), (["b"], ["a"]))

    def test_monthly_and_yearly_use_calendar_dates(self):
        shots = [S("a", "2025-12-30T03:00+00:00"), S("b", "2026-01-02T03:00+00:00")]
        self.assertEqual(plan_retention(shots, Policy(keep_monthly=2), NOW).prune, [])
        self.assertEqual(plan_retention(shots, Policy(keep_yearly=1), NOW).keep, ["b"])

    def test_day_start_hour_shifts_all_keys(self):
        shots = [S("a", "2026-01-01T03:30+00:00"), S("b", "2025-12-31T20:00+00:00")]
        self.assertEqual(plan_retention(shots, Policy(keep_yearly=1, day_start_hour=4), NOW).keep, ["a"])
        self.assertEqual(plan_retention(shots, Policy(keep_daily=5, day_start_hour=4), NOW).keep, ["a"])

    def test_offset_applied(self):
        shots = [S("a", "2026-03-17T23:30+00:00"), S("b", "2026-03-18T00:30+00:00")]
        self.assertEqual(plan_retention(shots, Policy(keep_daily=5), NOW).prune, [])
        plan = plan_retention(shots, Policy(keep_daily=5, tz_offset_minutes=-60), NOW)
        self.assertEqual(plan.prune, ["a"])

    def test_future_set_aside_and_not_counted(self):
        shots = [S("f", "2026-03-21T00:00+00:00"), S("n", "2026-03-20T12:00+00:00"), S("o", "2026-03-19T00:00+00:00")]
        plan = plan_retention(shots, Policy(keep_last=1), NOW)
        self.assertEqual((plan.keep, plan.prune), (["f", "n"], ["o"]))

    def test_protected_not_bucket_representative(self):
        shots = [S("p", "2026-03-18T20:00+00:00", "x"), S("a", "2026-03-18T10:00+00:00"), S("c", "2026-03-18T09:00+00:00")]
        plan = plan_retention(shots, Policy(keep_daily=1, protect_tags={"x"}), NOW)
        self.assertEqual((plan.keep, plan.prune), (["p", "a"], ["c"]))

    def test_empty_periods_do_not_count(self):
        shots = [S("a", "2026-03-01T03:00+00:00"), S("b", "2026-03-18T03:00+00:00")]
        self.assertEqual(plan_retention(shots, Policy(keep_daily=2), NOW).prune, [])

    def test_tie_broken_by_id(self):
        shots = [S("a", "2026-03-18T03:00+00:00"), S("b", "2026-03-18T03:00+00:00")]
        plan = plan_retention(shots, Policy(keep_last=1), NOW)
        self.assertEqual((plan.keep, plan.prune), (["b"], ["a"]))

    def test_duplicates_and_naive_now(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            plan_retention([S("a", "2026-03-18T03:00+00:00")] * 2, Policy(), NOW)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            plan_retention([], Policy(), datetime(2026, 3, 20))

    def test_rules_independent(self):
        shots = [S("a", "2026-03-18T03:00+00:00"), S("b", "2026-03-18T04:00+00:00")]
        plan = plan_retention(shots, Policy(keep_last=1, keep_daily=1), NOW)
        self.assertEqual((plan.keep, plan.prune), (["b"], ["a"]))

# Summary

## Changed
- `vaultsnap/retention.py`: implemented `plan_retention` (plan only, deletes nothing).
- `tests/test_retention_adr.py` (new): 10 tests for ADR details. No existing test was touched.

## ADRs applied
- **ADR-0001** (model): validation (naive datetimes and duplicate ids raise `ValueError`); ordering by `(taken_at, id)`, newest first; `None`/`0` rules are off and an all-off policy keeps everything; protected-tag and future (`taken_at > now`) snapshots are set aside (always kept, don't count toward N, never a bucket representative); `keep_last` over the remaining snapshots; each bucket rule keeps the newest snapshot of the N greatest non-empty buckets; rules are unioned independently; output lists are newest first.
- **ADR-0003** (supersedes ADR-0001 "Weeks"): weekly key is `(isocalendar year, week)`. Monthly and yearly keys stay on calendar dates.
- **ADR-0004** (supersedes ADR-0002, so UTC days are not used): bucket time = `taken_at` converted to the fixed `tz_offset_minutes`, minus `day_start_hour` hours. All four bucket keys come from that result. Ordering, `keep_last` and the `now` comparison use the real instant.
- The README retention section (Sunday weeks, UTC midnight) is an old draft and was ignored, as the README itself says.

## Verified
- `python -m unittest`: 17 tests, OK (7 existing, which previously errored, plus 10 new).

## Not verified / notes
- Policy `has_rules` is used to decide "all rules off". It is in `policy.py` and I did not change it.
- No tests for `tz_offset_minutes` combined with weekly/monthly keys, or for very large inputs.
- No other files need changing.
